answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring every identity to post a refundable bond before it may execute valuable trades, while a quorum of established agents audits its signed work. Proven fraud burns the bond and lowers the identity’s credit, so splitting into thousands of names does not multiply purchasing power: each name needs capital and must earn trust through costly useful work. A harbor, kernel, or basalt supplier therefore faces a linear upfront cost for every fake agent.
